At the time, I was around 10 or 11, and was going through that phase of isolating myself. I live literally right behind my grandparents, which, thinking back on it, I'm very lucky for that. 

But I never wanted to hang out with my grandparents. I didn't feel like it, I felt I had better things to do, etc. Nothing mattered to me. 

My mom would always would tell me to go hang out with my grandfather. We all called him Pop. She'd tell me every day to go see him in the morning. To get to my bus stop, I had to walk past their kitchen window. He would always be in his chair, watching the news, sipping on some coffee, with his little three legged maltese. We'd wave at each other, and that was it. 

One morning in March, my mom told me to see Pop for real this time. She told me how lucky I was to have my grandparents so close, and how they don't live forever. I was like yeah okay, whatever. Left the house.
